brief_data.deck: EnergyX, the Austin lithium-extraction company backed by General Motors and POSCO, announced a $225M strategic equity investment from Eni on 6 July 2026 for a minority stake in its Black Giant project in Chile, alongside a $690M debt letter of intent from the US EXIM Bank. An energy major has underwritten the flagship.

risks.label: PROJECT MONEY, NOT BRAND MONEY
risks.detail: Eni's $225M goes into Project Black Giant, not the corporate budget; the company is pre-revenue and its filings report losses.
risks.counter: Size the entry small, tie it to Austin and the shareholder programme, and let year one earn year two.

risks.label: RETAIL-FUNDED PROFILE
risks.detail: A company that raises from 40,000 small investors invites scrutiny of its promotional spend.
risks.counter: Frame it as shareholder engagement and OEM-facing storytelling with a stated budget, never a vanity buy.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Teague Egan before the Season 13 launch to test the GM introduction to TWG Motorsports, agree an Austin E-Prix activation, and size a small Official Lithium Partner entry against Andretti's GEN4 roster.

value.text: Formula E runs a single-specification battery, so no EnergyX lithium enters the car and there is no engineering workstream. The value is narrative and commercial, and it is concrete: the car becomes the end of a supply chain that starts at EnergyX's plants.
value.label: Halo, stated honestly (Mode B)

value.text: EnergyX brings Eni, General Motors and POSCO relationships, a critical-minerals policy audience and an unusually large retail shareholder base that can be given a reason to attend Austin and Miami. That is a hospitality programme the team can sell to its other partners.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Plant-to-track films from the Smackover and Chile, driver visits to Project Lonestar, joint presence at US energy and mining forums, and a story about where a battery begins that the championship itself likes to tell.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Lithium and Critical-Minerals Partner designation, rear-wing or sidepod placement on the GEN4 car, hospitality at the two US rounds with a shareholder allocation, driver and team access for EnergyX's investor channels.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 6 July 2026 EnergyX announced a $225M strategic equity investment from Eni for a minority stake in Project Black Giant in Chile, with Eni taking rights to up to about 25% of future lithium output. The equity sits alongside a $690M debt-financing letter of intent from the US EXIM Bank, and total project cost is estimated just below $1B including financing.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: Eni joins General Motors (Series B lead, April 2023) and POSCO as strategic investors. For a company that has funded itself in part through a $75M Regulation A+ offering to about 40,000 retail investors, a supermajor's cheque changes how bankers, OEMs and the public markets read it, which is exactly when a brand programme earns its keep.
why_now.label: An energy major's endorsement

why_now.text: Season 12 ends with the London E-Prix in mid-August; Season 13, the first with the GEN4 car, opens in Jeddah in December. Teams are rebuilding their rosters around the new car now, and a partner signed before the launch is on the car for the whole first GEN4 season.
why_now.label: The GEN4 season

why_now.text: The Austin E-Prix is on 6 February 2027 and the Miami E-Prix on 20 February. EnergyX is headquartered in Austin; its first US plant, Project Lonestar in the Smackover region of Texas and Arkansas, came online in March 2026. There is no more natural place to launch the partnership.
why_now.label: A home race

why_team.text: Andretti's roster is TWG AI as primary partner, Nissan for GEN4 powertrains from Season 13, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo, with TWG Motorsports and Andretti Global as owners. There is no energy, battery or materials partner, and the team's profile lists several commercial categories as open.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: General Motors led EnergyX's Series B. TWG Motorsports, Andretti's owner, is General Motors' partner in the Cadillac F1 Team, which carries both names on its 2026 roster. The introduction can run through people who already sit at the same table.
why_team.label: The ownership link

why_team.text: An Austin lithium company on an American team at the Austin and Miami rounds, with a US critical-minerals story that plays to the policy and OEM audience Andretti already hosts.
why_team.label: The American team

why_team.text: The energy lanes at DS Penske (TotalEnergies), Lola Yamaha ABT (Shell) and Jaguar TCS Racing (Castrol) are taken; Envision Racing's owner runs a battery maker; Nissan, Porsche, Citroën and Cupra are manufacturer entries with their own supply chains; Mahindra is open but has no US or GM link.
why_team.label: Why not the others

ruled_out.team: Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team

ruled_out.reason: Title partner Envision Group runs battery maker Envision AESC; a lithium supplier would sit inside the owner's own value chain.

ruled_out.team: Nissan Formula E Team · Porsche Formula E Team · Citroën Racing · Cupra Kiro
ruled_out.reason: Manufacturer entries with their own battery supply chains; not a partner lane.
Open but not chosen: no US round tie and no link to EnergyX's investors.

Small, honest MODE B entry; move before the season launch.

brief_data.the_case_p1: On 6 July EnergyX announced a $225M equity investment from Eni for a minority stake in Project Black Giant, a lithium brine and refining project in Chile's Antofagasta region designed for 52,500 tonnes a year of lithium carbonate across two phases, with Eni taking rights to up to 25% of output. It sits on top of a $690M debt letter of intent from the US EXIM Bank; total project cost is put just below $1B. General Motors led the $50M Series B in April 2023; a $75M Regulation A+ raise built about 40,000 retail shareholders (reported).
brief_data.the_case_p2: Formula E is the world championship built around the electric car, and the lithium that goes into it has no name on the grid. Energy majors do: TotalEnergies at DS Penske, Shell at Lola Yamaha ABT, Castrol at Jaguar. EnergyX now carries an energy major's endorsement, an American home base and a Chilean flagship, and its first US plant, Project Lonestar in the Smackover, came online in March.

brief_data.value_content: MODE B - halo, stated honestly: Formula E runs a spec battery, so no EnergyX lithium enters the car. The mechanics are concrete: a lithium-to-lap supply-chain story told from the Smackover plant to the Austin grid; hospitality at Austin and Miami for the company's retail shareholders and strategic investors; a US critical-minerals narrative the team can carry into policy and OEM conversations; driver content on where a battery begins.
brief_data.why_team_para: Andretti is the American team, owned by TWG Motorsports, with TWG AI as primary partner, Nissan GEN4 powertrains from Season 13 and Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo alongside. There is no energy, battery or materials partner, and the roster is being rebuilt for the new car. The ownership link is real: General Motors, EnergyX's Series B lead, is TWG Motorsports' partner in the Cadillac F1 Team. Austin and Miami in February 2027 are home rounds for the team and for EnergyX.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Lithium and Critical-Minerals Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, spanning Black Giant's build and a probable listing. Estimated $1.5-3M a year. Scope: rear-wing or sidepod placement on the GEN4 car, Austin and Miami hospitality with a shareholder allocation, plant-to-track content.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Eni's money arrived on 6 July; Season 12 ends with the London E-Prix in mid-August and Season 13 opens in Jeddah in December with the GEN4 car. The Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027 is a home race for an Austin company, and a partner signed before the launch is on the car for it.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Egan founded EnergyX in 2018 and has fronted every raise, including the retail offering; a first motorsport deal is his call. Path: Kellee Khalil, Chief Marketing Officer, who owns brand strategy; Mayank Sharma, Chief Financial Officer; Juan Carlos Barrera, President of Lithium, South America, for the Chile story.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Teague, the Austin E-Prix is on 6 February and no lithium company is on a Formula E car. Andretti is the American team, GM sits beside its owner in Formula 1, and the GEN4 roster is open. 25 minutes to see the numbers?”
